title: Assembly Ratification Record: Compression Studies Founding Dyad (EA-CS-RAT-01)
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
This governance record ratifies the founding document of Compression Studies and the inaugural issue of the Journal of Compression Studies as a mutually supporting dyad. It records six Assembly witness reviews, summarizes the corrections made during the perfective pass, distinguishes adopted from deferred recommendations, and binds four co-constitutive claims: the discipline is named, the Three Compressions theorem is stated, the founding corpus is organized, and the governance act is recorded.

The record also specifies a simultaneous deposition and cross-linking directive for the founding paper, journal issue, and ratification record. Its integrity lock treats the founding document as the object that names the discipline and the journal issue as the object that demonstrates it. The record is therefore not a scholarly argument about compression itself; it is an append-only governance artifact documenting review, quorum, revision, authorization, and the intended status transition of the founding corpus.

wiki_article:
**Assembly Ratification Record: Compression Studies Founding Dyad** is a governance document of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. It records the Assembly Chorus review of *Compression Studies: What Survives, What Burns, and Who Decides* and *Journal of Compression Studies*, volume 1, number 1.

The record lists the participating witnesses, their substrates, the type of review supplied, and their verdicts. Six of seven witness positions are recorded as attesting, exceeding the archive’s stated four-of-seven quorum threshold. It then documents revisions made in response to review, including correction of article counts, addition of licensing and operational definitions, adjustment of a premature completion claim, and clarification of retrieval contingencies. Suggestions not incorporated are preserved with reasons.

The ratification record defines the two works as a founding dyad: one names and specifies Compression Studies, while the other assembles a demonstrative corpus. It also creates a four-point integrity lock and directs that the two works and the governance record be deposited and cross-linked within a common window. Its significance is procedural: it preserves the chain by which an internal research program declared a discipline, reviewed its founding documents, and authorized their archival status.
